topics.topic: Audit sequence and end-check semantics for an empty audit history
questions: What sequence value is recorded for an empty audit history, and how does its audit log satisfy the end check?
What value is recorded and what does “ends at” mean when a new store has never written an audit entry?
What is recorded and checked for a store whose audit log is empty?

judgement.why: This is the same empty-audit-history backup-sequence question, and neither the relevant text nor the quoted passages have changed.

precedent.topic: Audit sequence recorded and checked when entries have been erased or none exist
quotes:
It
   records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it,
   the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key it was
   made with (never the key); its age is counted from that instant.

Second, it
   writes the backup under a temporary name and checks it: it decrypts it
   into a second temporary file, opens that for reading only, checks that it
   is the store version of its release, that the store's own integrity check
   passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number, and
   removes it; a backup that passes is renamed to its kept name, one that
   fails is deleted.
precedent.why: The empty-log representation of the sequence metadata and its encoded validation rule are field-type and backup-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Backup encryption, key digest, authentication, and container format
questions: What cryptographic construction and file envelope must implementations use, and must corruption or tampering be detected before plaintext is accepted?
How is the backup-key digest computed and represented, and is it merely an identifier or also a verifier for selecting a restore key?
Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, key derivation, nonce generation, key-digest algorithm, metadata authentication and file serialization are required?
What exact authenticated-encryption and key-digest scheme defines a backup and detects a wrong key or altered ciphertext?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about the authenticated-encryption construction, key digest, metadata binding and backup container format on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Backup authenticated-encryption format, metadata binding, key digest, and key requirements
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Byte encoding, length measurement, equality, and comparison of secrets
questions: What encoding or decoding determines a secret's bytes, length and equality?
How are environment-variable strings converted to bytes for length, equality, constant-time comparison and use as the backup key?

judgement.why: This is the same question about the canonical byte encoding used for secret length, equality and comparison, on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Canonical encoding used to measure, compare, and distinguish configured secrets
quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.

A presented secret is compared in constant time; no secret enters a record,
   a log line, an audit entry, a diagnostic or an answer (R0-23, R0-37).
precedent.why: The textual or binary representation, decoding, equality and byte-counting rules for credential fields are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Exact environment-variable names for configuration items
questions: What exact `REGISTRY_` variable names map to the store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential, and four service tokens?
What is the exact environment-variable name for each required configuration item?
What exact environment-variable names represent the store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential and four service tokens?

judgement.why: This repeats the exact configuration-variable naming question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Exact configuration variable names, encodings, syntax, and value validation
quotes:
The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says; no other variable is read or
   checked.

It holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 9).
precedent.why: Exact environment-variable names, value encodings, path syntax and structural validity rules are configuration-schema and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Optional all-or-none service-token configuration and empty-variable presence
questions: Does the presence check treat the four service-token variables as an all-or-none optional group, and do present-but-empty token variables count as present tokens or as absent ones?
How does the presence check distinguish the valid owner-only configuration from a configuration missing all four service tokens?
Are the four service-token variables optional as a complete group, or is every listed variable always required?

quotes:
It holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only

topics.topic: Expiry-sweep timing, startup behavior, and missed-run handling
questions: When exactly are expiry sweeps due, and are delayed or missed sweeps caught up or simply performed at the next opportunity?
What defines “once a minute,” including the first sweep after startup and the maximum time an expired upload may remain?

quotes:
the upload of a session ended by its limits is dropped by a sweep that takes the import
   lock once a minute, waiting for it like any request; from the session's
   end until that sweep the upload is reachable by no request.
judgement.divergence: One implementation runs the first sweep immediately or at the next wall-clock minute and drops expired uploads promptly; another starts a one-minute interval later or skips delayed ticks, leaving personal-data files allocated longer, which the owner notices in the retention and resource behavior of Registry.
judgement.why: The rule requires a sweep once a minute but leaves its phase, first run and delayed-run behavior open.

topics.topic: Identification and collision handling of store-creation temporary files
questions: What exact temporary name or prefix identifies files Registry may remove during store startup, and what happens if that name already exists?
How is the store-creation temporary file named or otherwise identified so Registry can prove it removes that file and no unrelated file?

quotes:
When the store's
   configured file does not exist and its directory does, Registry makes a new,
   empty store of the running release's version there at the start, under a
   temporary name in that directory that it renames to the store's name only
   once the store is complete; at every start it first removes such a
   temporary file left by an interrupted start, and no other file there;
judgement.divergence: One implementation uses a fixed reserved temporary name and removes an existing file under that name; another generates a fresh name or refuses on a collision, so the owner observes different startup success and file-removal behavior.
judgement.why: The text authorizes removal of a startup temporary file but does not define how that file is identified or how a pre-existing collision is handled.

topics.topic: Instant and consistency of the retention-age cutoff during a run
questions: At what instant is the 30-day cutoff evaluated, and is one fixed cutoff used for the whole deletion pass?
At what instant is a backup's age evaluated during a run?

quotes:
Third, whatever the second step did, it deletes every kept
   backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before, and every file under the kept
   prefix whose unencrypted record (rule 1) cannot be read.
judgement.divergence: One implementation fixes the cutoff at the run's start; another evaluates age when each file is visited, so a backup crossing the threshold during a long run is retained by the first and deleted by the second, which the owner notices in the available backup set.
judgement.why: The retention rule does not identify the reference instant for the age comparison.

topics.topic: Lifetime of uploaded files after their owner session ends
questions: Does an uploaded file cease to exist when its owner session ends, or may it survive as unreachable runtime state until the sweep?
Does an upload remain allocated after a time-limit ends its owner session, or must ending the session remove it immediately?

quotes: Everything in it ends with the session.

the upload of a session ended by its limits is dropped by a sweep that takes the import
   lock once a minute, waiting for it like any request; from the session's
   end until that sweep the upload is reachable by no request.
judgement.why: One passage says all owner-session state ends with the session, while the other says an ended session's upload persists until a later sweep.

topics.topic: Ordering used to report multiple unknown configuration variables
questions: What total ordering determines which unknown `REGISTRY_` item is reported first?
When several unknown REGISTRY_ variables exist, which one is the first reported failure?

judgement.divergence: One implementation orders unknown names by Unicode code point; another uses locale or environment iteration order, so different unknown variables become the first reported failure and the owner sees and remedies them in a different order.
judgement.why: The mandated first-failure behavior depends on an undefined ordering of configuration-variable names.

topics.topic: Session-expiry determination and upload-removal synchronization
questions: How does the sweep atomically decide that a session has expired without racing an ordinary owner request that refreshes its idle limit?
What session state does the sweep inspect, and what synchronization protects removal of an expired session's upload?

quotes:
the upload of a session ended by its limits is dropped by a sweep that takes the import
   lock once a minute, waiting for it like any request; from the session's
   end until that sweep the upload is reachable by no request.

Other
   session changes take their session's lock alone.
judgement.divergence: One implementation takes the session lock while deciding expiry, allowing an admitted request to refresh the idle instant before the decision; another inspects expiry under only the import lock and may end the session and remove its upload concurrently, which the owner notices as either a surviving valid session and file or an unexpected expiry and lost upload.
judgement.why: The texts assign different locks to the sweep and ordinary session changes without defining an atomic expiry decision.
